title: The Partial Alternating Binomial Sum and Pascal Telescoping
content: `altPartial f m` = Σ_{j=0}^m (-1)^j C(f,j) is the truncation of the binomial expansion of (1−1)^f. `altPartial_zero` gives A(0,m) = 1 (only the j=0 term survives). `altPartial_succ` is the crux identity: A(f+1,m) = (-1)^m C(f,m), proved by induction on m using Pascal's rule C(f+1,m+1) = C(f,m) + C(f,m+1) (Nat.choose_succ_succ), which telescopes the alternating partial sum to a SINGLE term. Its sign (-1)^m and non-negative magnitude C(f,m) are the entire source of the Bonferroni one-sidedness — every subsequent step just exposes this term per permutation.

title: The Truncated Sieve in Subset Form
content: `fixCard σ` is the number of fixed points of a permutation; `truncSieve n m` = Σ_{k=0}^m (-1)^k C(n,k)(n-k)! is the derangement sieve truncated after the size-m layer. `truncSieve_eq_subset_sum` rewrites each binomial term C(n,k)(n-k)! as the sum over size-k subsets t of the signed crux count (-1)^|t|·#{σ fixing every point of t}, directly reusing the parent's `card_fixesOn` (= (n−|t|)!). This recasts the truncation as a double sum over (subset, permutation) pairs — the form on which the Fubini swap operates.

title: The Fubini Reindexing Over Permutations
content: `truncSieve_eq_sum_altPartial`: exchanging the order of summation (Finset.sum_comm) in the subset form yields B(n,m) = Σ_σ A(f_σ, m), summing over all permutations. The key observation is that for a FIXED permutation σ, the subsets t all of whose points σ fixes are exactly the subsets of σ's fixed-point set, of which there are C(f_σ, k) of size k — so σ's total contribution is Σ_{k≤m}(-1)^k C(f_σ,k) = A(f_σ,m). This converts a statement about truncated alternating SUMS into a statement about each PERMUTATION's fixed-point count, where the Pascal-telescoped sign becomes visible.
mathContext: $B(n,m)=\sum_{\sigma\in\mathrm{Perm}(\mathrm{Fin}\,n)}A(f_\sigma,m)$, since $\sigma$ fixes $C(f_\sigma,k)$ subsets of size $k$ pointwise.

title: Isolating Derangements and the Core Sign
content: `card_deranged_filter` / `numDerangements_eq_indicator_sum` identify the derangements as the f_σ = 0 permutations (card_derangements_eq_numDerangements), so D_n = Σ_σ [f_σ = 0]. `truncSieve_sub_numDerangements` writes B(n,m) − D_n = Σ_σ (A(f_σ,m) − [f_σ = 0]); `neg_one_pow_mul_term_nonneg` shows each term times (-1)^m is non-negative — 0 for derangements (A(0,m) = 1 cancels the indicator), and (-1)^m·(-1)^m C(f_σ−1,m) = C(f_σ−1,m) ≥ 0 for non-derangements (via altPartial_succ). Summing gives `neg_one_pow_mul_truncSieve_sub_nonneg`: (-1)^m (B(n,m) − D_n) = Σ_{f_σ≥1} C(f_σ−1,m) ≥ 0.

title: The Bonferroni Inequalities (and the n = 4 Ladder)
content: Splitting the core sign by parity (Even.neg_one_pow / Odd.neg_one_pow) gives the Bonferroni inequalities: `bonferroni_even` — D_n ≤ B(n,m) when m is even (the truncation over-counts), and `bonferroni_odd` — B(n,m) ≤ D_n when m is odd (it under-counts). `truncSieve_self` confirms B(n,n) = D_n via the parent's exact sieve identity, so the bounds become equality at full depth. The concrete examples verify the n = 4 bracketing ladder with kernel `decide`: B(4,0)=24 ≥ B(4,2)=12 ≥ D_4=9 ≥ B(4,3)=8 ≥ B(4,1)=0, i.e. even truncations above and odd truncations below the true count 9.
mathContext: $m$ even $\Rightarrow D_n\le B(n,m)$; $m$ odd $\Rightarrow B(n,m)\le D_n$; $B(n,n)=D_n$. For $n=4$: $24\ge12\ge9\ge8\ge0$.
